        How Caveat Red works

        Help

        A local workflow for documenting uncertainty, evidence, and the next verification step.

        1

        Assess systematically

        Use the checklist to review technology, financial, commercial, leadership, operational, and transparency concerns.

        2

        Keep a source trail

        Record exact claims, sources, evidence limits, and whether each item supports or contradicts the claim.

        3

        Prioritize verification

        Use severity × likelihood to decide what needs attention next, then document focused follow-up questions.

        What does a red flag mean here?

        A red flag is a reason to investigate, not evidence of fraud or wrongdoing. The app separates verified findings, contradictory information, unknowns, and resolved concerns.

        How are priority scores calculated?

        Priority = severity × likelihood, on a 1–5 scale. Evidence confidence remains separate so a higher score never implies certainty.

        How do I start a new investigation?

        Use the quiet “Create an investigation” link on Overview or the New investigation button in Settings. Add the company, industry, stage, and review purpose; the app creates an empty local record and opens it immediately.

        What is the difference between a finding, claim, and evidence?

        A claim is a statement to verify. Evidence is the source material that supports, limits, or contradicts it. A finding records a specific concern that needs follow-up, with its priority and status kept separate from the underlying facts.

        How do I answer or close a follow-up request?

        Open Research, select Follow-ups, then choose Answer beside an open request. Record the response, supporting source, and outcome. Choose “Closed without answer” when the request will not be answered.

        How does the checklist affect the final report?

        The checklist tracks what has been reviewed and highlights where coverage is incomplete. Use its results to decide which evidence-backed findings and open questions should appear in the report; it does not turn an unanswered checklist item into a conclusion.

        How do I export and back up my data?

        Select Export on Overview, Export JSON on Report, or Export data in Settings to download a JSON copy of the active investigation. The Report page also offers a Markdown export for sharing a readable working draft.

        What does local-only mean?

        Records are stored in this browser profile and are not sent to a server. Browser clearing, changing profiles, or moving devices can remove them, so export a JSON backup regularly when the record matters.

        What belongs in a report?

        Reports should distinguish evidence-backed findings, unresolved questions, and information gaps. Avoid conclusions that exceed the available record.
